history.prompt: Clean isometric cutaway illustration of an automated warehouse aisle on a polished concrete floor. A fleet of identical unbranded autonomous mobile robots is arranged in a rigid symmetrical grid, rows receding toward a far steel rack where one blank paper invoice lies. Each robot has a matte grey polymer chassis with safety-yellow trim, black drive wheels, and visible battery bay seams. One directional hard light from the upper left casts long shadows across the concrete. Graphite, bone white, and safety yellow palette. Thin consistent line weight, unlabelled, generous empty margin, one-point perspective down the aisle.

style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: Telephoto 200mm long-lens photograph down a warehouse aisle, deep depth of field, flat compressed perspective stacking dozens of identical unbranded autonomous warehouse robots — matte polymer shrouds, brushed steel masts, scuffed safety-yellow corners — parked in long charging rows, overlapping layer upon layer into one dense mass. Hard low sunlight rakes from the left through high clerestory windows, throwing long parallel contact shadows across the polished concrete floor; crisp crystal-clear air, no haze, no people. Palette of safety yellow, graphite and concrete grey, galvanised racking receding behind. Extreme asymmetric framing: the stacked robot rows fill the right two-thirds, empty aisle floor and steel columns holding the left. Fine film grain, deep industrial contrast.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, numbers, watermarks, logos
rationale: The protagonist is a fleet, not one machine, and the news is its scale: dozens of identical units bought together returning together as one block. Telephoto compression physically stacks the rows into a single mass, so the reader feels the wave nobody reserves for. With flatlay, collage, night and cinematic still used most recently, a compressed industrial photograph is the right register for warehouse capex.
cue: The machines arrive together, age together and fail together
subject: A fleet of identical unbranded autonomous warehouse robots parked in long rows down a warehouse aisle
core_thesis: A robot fleet bought in a single year comes back as one renewal bill roughly eight times the annual charge, and a reserve funded at the original invoice covers only about three quarters of the compounded replacement price across an 8.3-year life — so the second purchase is a capital plan, not a forecast.
core_conflict: Machines that arrive together, age together and fail together produce one synchronized capital wave at year 8.3, colliding with capital plans that only ever priced and reserved for the first invoice while the equipment price index compounds.
composition: Extreme asymmetry: telephoto-compressed rows of identical robots stacked in overlapping layers commanding the right two-thirds, with high negative space of empty aisle and steel columns holding the left third.
